title: I Applied the Overnight Package Fridge Rule to the Partner Who Invented It

parts.text: I clocked into the mailroom at 6:52 a.m. and the overnight fridge was already a Tetris of someone else's Whole Foods bags. The laminated rule on the door, signed by Partner Hale, said: CLIENT PACKAGES ONLY. NO PERSONAL FOOD AFTER 7 P.M. I was twenty-nine, records clerk, holding a FedEx sleeve that had to stay cold until 9. Hale's yogurt sat on the vaccine-shaped ice pack meant for the sleeve. "That's my breakfast," he said, already peeling the foil. I pointed at his own sign. He laughed. "Partners are clients of the firm." I photographed the yogurt on the ice pack, the sign, and the tracking number. Then I moved his breakfast to the regular fridge and logged a chain-of-custody note. At 7:04 the managing partner asked why Hale's name was on a temperature excursion ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The managing partner can see Hale's yogurt on the ice pack meant for the client sleeve.

social.video_title: He put yogurt on the client ice pack — Part 1/2
social.description: Overnight fridge, a partner's breakfast, and a rule he laminated himself. I logged the excursion. Would you have moved the yogurt?

parts.text: Hale called it a joke until the client asked for the temperature log. I printed the ticket, the sign, and the photo. Facilities replaced the ice pack. Hale ate room-temperature yogurt at his desk and told associates the rule was always about optics. Optics is a word partners use when a photo exists. Mailroom policy now has a second line: PARTNERS ARE NOT CLIENTS OF THE FRIDGE. I keep the FedEx sleeve on a labeled tray. Hale brown-bags. The overnight fridge hums like it finally got the memo.
